content: If a strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the dose of erdafitinib, provided there are no drug-related toxicities. Efavirenz increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by reducing their metabolism, potentially leading to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ergonovine and ergotamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, but it can also increase ergotamine levels by reducing its metabolism. This interaction may lead to vasospasm and ischemia; therefore, avoid or use an alternative drug. Efavirenz and eribulin both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring or the use of alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of erlotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and close monitoring. Erythromycin base increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while efavirenz decreases erythromycin base levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs should be considered, or close monitoring is required. Similar interactions occur with erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate, all of which increase efavirenz levels, while efavirenz decreases their levels. These combinations also prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution or alternative therapies. Efavirenz increases escitalopram levels via CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases them via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so caution and monitoring are advised. Efavirenz and esketamine intranasal increase each other's toxicity through sedation, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Efavirenz decreases eslicarbazepine acetate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, efavirenz decreases esomeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases them via CYP2C19 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Efavirenz decreases estradiol levels, including vaginal formulations, as well as conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate, by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are recommended. Efavirenz decreases eszopiclone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs increase sedation, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases ethinyl estradiol levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. Efavirenz decreases ethosuximide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Efavirenz increases ethotoin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases etonogestrel and etoposide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Efavirenz increases etrasimod levels in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers when coadministered with CYP2C8 inhibitors, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases etravirine levels by increasing its metabolism, and this combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz decreases eucalyptus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Efavirenz decreases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and this combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz decreases exemestane levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring. For patients on exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, a dose of 50 mg daily after a meal is recommended. Fedratinib increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while efavirenz decreases fedratinib levels. Alternative drugs are recommended, as the effect of strong CYP3A4 inducers on fedratinib has not been studied. Efavirenz decreases felbamate and felodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Efavirenz decreases fentanyl levels, potentially leading to withdrawal in dependent patients, while both drugs increase sedation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Efavirenz decreases fesoterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Efavirenz increases fexinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while fexinidazole decreases efavirenz levels via CYP2B6 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases finasteride levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Efavirenz decreases finerenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz and fingolimod both prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz and flecainide also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval, though fluconazole increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz decreases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though fludrocortisone decreases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz increases flurbiprofen and fluvastatin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, necessitating caution. Fluvoxamine increases efavirenz levels via CYP2B6 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while fosamprenavir increases efavirenz levels. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Efavirenz decreases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while fosaprepitant increases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz increases fosphenytoin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while fosphenytoin decreases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz decreases fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases fostemsavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and this combination is contraindicated. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz decreases fruquintinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz and ganaxolone increase sedation, while efavirenz decreases ganaxolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz decreases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification. Efavirenz and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz and gilteritinib also prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz and givinostat prolong the QTc interval, requiring ECG monitoring if coadministration is unavoidable. Efavirenz decreases glasdegib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing therapeutic efficacy. Efavirenz and goserelin both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz and granisetron also prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Grapefruit increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Griseofulvin decreases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Efavirenz decreases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification. Efavirenz decreases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz and histrelin both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers coadministered with hydrocodone may increase hydrocodone levels, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Efavirenz decreases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though hydrocortisone decreases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz and hydroxyzine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz increases ibuprofen levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases idelalisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and idelalisib increases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz increases ifosfamide toxicity via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz decreases imatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unclear. Efavirenz increases imipramine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz and indacaterol both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while indinavir increases efavirenz levels. Efavirenz decreases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases irinotecan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring alternative drugs. Efavirenz decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and this combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval, requiring alternative drugs. Isoniazid increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases isosorbide dinitrate and mononitrate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases isradipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Istradefylline increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while efavirenz decreases istradefylline levels. Avoid coadministration of istradefylline with efavirenz.
